subject: Data Processing Annex, SCCs & DPIA scope for State DOT RFP
messages:
From: John Miller <john.miller@statetransit.gov>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@statetransit.gov>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP request — DPA, SCCs, DPIA scope

Sean —

Thanks for engaging on the RFP (State DOT - Intelligent Corridor Pilot). Procurement asked that vendors provide an explicit Data Processing Annex (DPA) that incorporates the state's SCC requirement, a copy of your latest SOC 2 report (redacted is OK), and completion of the SIG/CAIQ snapshot by 05/15 to support our security evaluation.

Separately, the state's privacy office requires vendors to provide a short DPIA scope memo describing what processing activities are in-scope for the pilot (especially around location telemetry and camera-derived metrics), where data will be stored, and whether any biometric or PII-derived profiling is performed. The DPIA can be high level but must identify categories of data, subprocessors, and retention defaults.

Questions we need answered:
- Can Redwood execute the state's SCCs (we will provide the state's annex text) or do you propose the standard EU SCCs + state annex?
- Where would customer data be stored (region/column of cloud provider)? Any option for in-state residency?
- Can you provide SOC2 and SIG/CAIQ artifacts by 05/15?
- Do you have a sample DPA we can review/mark up?

Appreciate a quick confirmation and an ETA on the artifacts.

Regards,
John Miller
Senior Procurement Officer
State Department of Transportation

--
State DOT Procurement | RFP# 2026-IC-07

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP request — DPA, SCCs, DPIA scope

John —

Thanks — we can support the RFP requirements and will get you the artifacts. Quick answers up-front so Procurement has what it needs immediately:

- SCCs: Redwood is able to sign the state's SCC annex in addition to the standard EU SCCs. We typically accept state-specific annex text subject to limited legal carve-outs; Vivek (cc'd) will confirm.
- Data residency: Hosted customers may choose region (US/EU/APAC). We can commit to US-only regional storage for this engagement; true in-state residency (physical hardware inside the state) is not part of our hosted offering without a dedicated/private deployment — we can discuss Dedicated if required.
- Artifacts ETA: SOC2 (redacted) and CAIQ/SIG snapshot by end of day 05/12; DPA template attached for your review.
- DPIA scope: We'll send a short scope memo that lists categories of processing and suggested retention defaults; we can collaborate with your privacy team to finalize.

Attaching: Redwood DPA template (stapled with default SCC references).

Proposed next step: 30-min call with John + Procurement + our legal (Vivek) and Monica (Customer Security) tomorrow 05/11 at 10:00 AM PT to walk the SCC annex and DPIA scope. Does that work?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive — Public Sector
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-DPA-Template.docx (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: State DOT SCC annex — redline summary

Team —

I reviewed the state's SCC annex text that John sent. High-level notes for the DPA redline:

1) Subprocessors: we should accept a dynamic subprocessor list with 30 days' notice + ability to object for critical subprocessors. For state procurement, propose 14 days to align with their timelines.
2) Security measures: the annex asks for FIPS 140-2 KMS attestations — we can commit to using cloud KMS with FIPS boundary, but need a carve-out for multi-tenant hosted tenants where HSM-backed keys require Dedicated.
3) Restriction on international transfers: propose EU SCCs + state annex; do not accept a state-unique carve that prevents transfers necessary for our CDNs/edge caching. Suggest an explicit exceptions clause for operational routing.
4) DPIA collaboration: we will produce a DPIA scope memo; however, responsibility for conducting the formal DPIA (if required by the state's privacy office) should remain with the data controller (State DOT). We can provide the processing details and support evidence.

I've prepared a redline of our standard DPA with annotations for the points above — attached. Monica, please prepare SOC2/CAIQ + a short DPIA scope memo we can send to procurement. Lauren, heads up in case procurement pushes for an expedited negotiated DPA.

Vivek
General Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: State-DOT-DPA-Redline-by-Redwood.docx (attachment stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@statetransit.gov>, Procurement Team <procurement@statetransit.gov>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP request — DPA, SCCs, DPIA scope (artifacts attached)

John / Procurement —

Following up with the artifacts we discussed. Attached are: redacted SOC 2 Type II (2025), Redwood SIG-lite answers, and a machine-readable CAIQ snapshot. Also included below is a short DPIA scope memo tailored to the Intelligent Corridor Pilot.

Attachments:
- Redwood_SOC2_Type2-2025-redacted.pdf (redacted report)
- Redwood-SIG-Lite-Response-2026.xlsx
- Redwood-CAIQ-Snapshot-2026.json

DPIA scope (summary):
- Processing categories: vehicle telemetry (anonymized travel times, GPS traces aggregated to corridor level), infrastructure telemetry (sensor health, occupancy counts), and optional camera-derived metrics (non-identifying counts and anonymized density heatmaps). No facial recognition or identity profiling by default.
- Data categories: pseudonymized device IDs, timestamps, aggregated counts; no name/SSN unless explicitly provided by the DOT.
- Subprocessors: cloud provider (GCP/AWS depending on region), CDN provider, analytics monitoring (SaaS). Full subprocessor list link is available.
- Retention defaults: 180 days for raw telemetry; aggregated metrics retained 5 years for trend analysis. Retention is configurable in contract.
- Data residency: Redwood hosted customers can restrict processing to US regions; we cannot guarantee physical in-state hardware unless the customer purchases Dedicated capacity.

Quick answers to your checklist:
- SCCs: Redwood accepts standard EU SCCs and will incorporate the state's annex with the exceptions noted by legal (see redline).
- SOC2 & CAIQ: attached.
- DPA: Sean shared our template; Vivek has provided redlines. We can provide an executed DPA via DocuSign once the state confirms the annex language.

Links: SOC2 redacted (attached), CAIQ/CAIQ JSON hosted: https://drive.google.com/StateDOT/RFP-2026-Security/CAIQ-Redwood
DocuSign DPA link will be sent once final DPA text is agreed.

Let me know if you want an inventory of subprocessors broken down by region — happy to provide. Can we get the state's DPIA questionnaire (if any) so we can populate the full form?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Security — Redwood Inference

--
